notes.text: Security update for ImageMagick
notes.title: Title of the patch

notes.text:
This update for ImageMagick fixes the following issues:

- CVE-2026-93586: use-after-free in the `ImagesToBlob` method can lead to a process crash (bsc#1281912).
- CVE-2026-106565: a missing end-of-file check while reading bzip2-compressed image data can cause an infinite loop
  (bsc#1284662).
- CVE-2026-106567: a crafted PSD file can trigger an integer-conversion error in the PSD decoder, causing an infinite
  loop and DoS (bsc#1284664).
- CVE-2026-106568: a crafted XMP profile embedded in an image can cause the profile parser to enter an infinite loop
  (bsc#1284665).
- CVE-2026-106571: a crafted local call to the GetVirtualPixels API can trigger an integer calculation error and write
  beyond a heap buffer, crashing the server process (bsc#1284668).
- CVE-2026-106572: a missing recursion-depth check in the CALS decoder allows a crafted CALS image to exhaust the call
  stack and terminate the process (bsc#1284669).
- CVE-2026-106577: unescaped or untrimmed values can inject code into output generated by PostScript coders
  (bsc#1284675).
- CVE-2026-106579: a crafted image can bypass an ImageMagick security policy that uses coder as its domain, potentially
  allowing data prohibited by the policy to be read (bsc#1284678).
- CVE-2026-106580: a missing security-policy check in the CUT encoder allows a crafted local encoding operation to read
  data that policy should deny and can also cause a crash (bsc#1284680).
- CVE-2026-107208: a crafted XMP profile can reach a recursion limit that is handled as a fatal condition instead of an
  ordinary exception, terminating the image-processing process (bsc#1284681).
- CVE-2026-107209: when ImageMagick is built without Cairo support, a crafted RSVG image that reaches a resource limit
  can cause a crash (bsc#1284682).
- CVE-2026-107210: a crafted highly compressed MAT image can make the MAT decoder create temporary files larger than the
  configured security-policy limit (bsc#1284683).
- CVE-2026-109259: Information disclosure via crafted TGA image (bsc#1285071).
- CVE-2026-109260: Denial of Service via memory leak in PNG encoder (bsc#1285071).
- CVE-2026-109261: Denial of Service via memory leak in GIF encoder (bsc#1285071).
- CVE-2026-109262: Denial of Service via memory leak in SVG encoder (bsc#1285071).
- CVE-2026-109263: Denial of Service via memory leak in YUV encoder (bsc#1285071).
- CVE-2026-109266: XML injection vulnerability in the CIP encoder (bsc#1285071).
- CVE-2026-109269: Information disclosure via crafted JPEG file (bsc#1285071).
- CVE-2026-109273: Information disclosure via crafted PostScript file (bsc#1285071).
- CVE-2026-109275: Code injection via crafted MVG file (bsc#1285071).
- CVE-2026-109276: Denial of Service via temporary file leak in JNG decoder (bsc#1285071).

notes.text: ImageMagick is free and open-source software used for editing and manipulating digital images. Prior to 7.1.2-32 and 6.9.13-57, a missing end-of-file check while reading bzip2-compressed image data can cause an infinite loop and exhaust processing resources. This issue is fixed in versions 7.1.2-32 and 6.9.13-57.

notes.text: ImageMagick is free and open-source software used for editing and manipulating digital images. Prior to 7.1.2-32 and 6.9.13-57, a crafted PSD file can trigger an integer-conversion error in the PSD decoder on 32-bit builds, causing an infinite loop and denial of service. This issue is fixed in versions 7.1.2-32 and 6.9.13-57.

notes.text: ImageMagick is free and open-source software used for editing and manipulating digital images. Prior to 7.1.2-32 and 6.9.13-57, a crafted XMP profile embedded in an image can cause the profile parser to enter an infinite loop, preventing image processing from completing. This issue is fixed in versions 7.1.2-32 and 6.9.13-57.

notes.text: ImageMagick is free and open-source software used for editing and manipulating digital images. Prior to 6.9.13-56 and 7.1.2-31, a crafted local call to the GetVirtualPixels API can trigger an integer calculation error and write beyond a heap buffer, crashing the server process. This issue is fixed in versions 6.9.13-56 and 7.1.2-31.

notes.text: ImageMagick is free and open-source software used for editing and manipulating digital images. Prior to 7.1.2-30 and 6.9.13-55, a missing recursion-depth check in the CALS decoder allows a crafted CALS image to exhaust the call stack and terminate the process. This issue is fixed in versions 7.1.2-30 and 6.9.13-55.

notes.text: ImageMagick is free and open-source software used for editing and manipulating digital images. Prior to 7.1.2-31 and 6.9.13-56, a crafted image can bypass an ImageMagick security policy that uses coder as its domain, potentially allowing data prohibited by the policy to be read. This issue is fixed in versions 7.1.2-31 and 6.9.13-56.

notes.text: ImageMagick is free and open-source software used for editing and manipulating digital images. Prior to 7.1.2-31 and 6.9.13-56, a missing security-policy check in the CUT encoder allows a crafted local encoding operation to read data that policy should deny and can also cause a crash. This issue is fixed in versions 7.1.2-31 and 6.9.13-56.

notes.text: ImageMagick is free and open-source software used for editing and manipulating digital images. Prior to 7.1.2-30 and 6.9.13-55, a crafted XMP profile can reach a recursion limit that is handled as a fatal condition instead of an ordinary exception, terminating the image-processing process. This issue is fixed in versions 7.1.2-30 and 6.9.13-55.

notes.text: ImageMagick is free and open-source software used for editing and manipulating digital images. Prior to 7.1.2-30 and 6.9.13-55, when ImageMagick is built without Cairo support, a crafted RSVG image that reaches a resource limit can cause the RSVG decoder to free image state twice and then use freed memory, crashing the process. This issue is fixed in versions 7.1.2-30 and 6.9.13-55.

notes.text: ImageMagick is free and open-source software used for editing and manipulating digital images. Prior to 7.1.2-30 and 6.9.13-55, a crafted highly compressed MAT image can make the MAT decoder create temporary files larger than the configured security-policy limit, bypassing resource restrictions and consuming excessive disk space. This issue is fixed in versions 7.1.2-30 and 6.9.13-55.

notes.text: ImageMagick before 6.9.13-57 and 7.x before 7.1.2-32 contains a memory leak in the PNG encoder, which does not release allocated memory when libpng initialization fails. Attackers who can repeatedly trigger PNG encoding operations in which libpng initialization fails can exhaust memory and cause a denial of service.

notes.text: ImageMagick before 6.9.13-57 and 7.x before 7.1.2-32 contains a memory leak in the GIF encoder because allocated memory is not released when color quantization fails during encoding. Attackers can supply images whose GIF conversion causes quantization to fail, leaking memory with each attempt and degrading availability.

notes.text: ImageMagick before 6.9.13-57 and 7.x before 7.1.2-32 contains a memory leak in the SVG encoder (WriteSVGImage) that fails to release allocated memory when handling crafted images. Attackers can supply crafted image files that are processed by the SVG encoder to leak memory and cause a denial of service through resource consumption.

notes.text: ImageMagick before 6.9.13-57 and 7.x before 7.1.2-32 contains a memory leak in the YUV encoder, which fails to release allocated memory when a specific operation fails. Attackers can supply crafted input that triggers the failing encoder operation, leaking memory and potentially exhausting resources to cause a denial of service.

notes.text: ImageMagick before 6.9.13-57 and 7.x before 7.1.2-32 contains an XML injection vulnerability in the CIP encoder, which does not properly escape input-derived data when writing Cisco IP Phone XML output. Attackers can supply a crafted file that, when converted to CIP format, injects arbitrary markup into the generated XML.

notes.text: ImageMagick before 6.9.13-57 and 7.x before 7.1.2-32 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in the JPEG decoder, which performs a read that exposes uninitialized memory when handling crafted input. Attackers can supply a crafted JPEG file for processing to disclose uninitialized memory contents.

notes.text: ImageMagick before 6.9.13-57 and 7.x before 7.1.2-32 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in the PostScript decoder, which allocates a buffer one byte longer than the data it decoded. Attackers can supply a crafted PostScript file to expose a single uninitialized byte of memory contents.

notes.text: ImageMagick before 6.9.13-57 and 7.x before 7.1.2-32 contains a code injection vulnerability in the MVG decoder when a PostScript renderer is used. Attackers can supply a crafted MVG file that, when decoded, injects code into the PostScript rendering path.

notes.text: ImageMagick before 6.9.13-57 and 7.x before 7.1.2-32 contains an incomplete cleanup flaw in the JNG decoder that fails to remove temporary files when processing crafted input. Attackers can submit crafted JNG files for processing to repeatedly leak temporary files, consuming disk space and degrading availability.

notes.text: ImageMagick is free and open-source software used for editing and manipulating digital images. Prior to versions 6.9.13-48 and 7.1.2-23, when using LZMA compression in the MIFF encoder an out of bounds write can occur due to a missing check. This issue has been patched in versions 6.9.13-48 and 7.1.2-23.

notes.text: ImageMagick before 7.1.2-31 and before 6.9.13-56 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in the ImagesToBlob method, caused by a pointer that is not updated correctly. Exploitation may result in a limited availability impact (e.g., a crash of the affected process). The issue is fixed in versions 7.1.2-31 and 6.9.13-56.
